Messages.Author: Jonathan Aiello
Messages.Body:
THE THIRD TRADITION: PROGENY
   
   What clan does the progeny belong to?  We've come up with
   three different options:
      1) the clan of the progenitor
      2) Caitiff
      3) no clan

HAVEN UNCOVERED/BUM'S RUSH

   Does being attacked via one of these cards tap the defending
   vampire?

TELEPAHTIC COUNTER

   If the bleed is reduced to zero, then the bleed is considered
   unsuccessful.  Is the bleeding vampire tapped?

MINION TAP

   Is this card a one-shot deal?  IE, you play it and you get to
   move the blood one time only.  Or do you play it on a particular
   vampire and then do you get to move blood every turn?

Thanks for any info.

--

Messages.Author: Rick Mc Leod
Messages.Body:
(Jonathan Aiello) writes:
>
>THE THIRD TRADITION: PROGENY
>   
>   What clan does the progeny belong to?  We've come up with
>   three different options:
>      1) the clan of the progenitor
>      2) Caitiff
>      3) no clan

Good question. Would also apply to The Embrace (usable by all kindred).
Going by the Masquerade, it would have to be (1). Princes aren't
likely to be thin blooded, and thus produce Caitiff.

>HAVEN UNCOVERED/BUM'S RUSH
>
>   Does being attacked via one of these cards tap the defending
>   vampire?

Absolutely NOT. If another vampire block's the rush, the blocker
taps. Actions tap. Blocks tap. Voting doesn't.

>TELEPAHTIC COUNTER
>
>   If the bleed is reduced to zero, then the bleed is considered
>   unsuccessful.  Is the bleeding vampire tapped?

Yes. The bleed is unsuccessful, but the action still taps the bleeder.

>MINION TAP
>
>   Is this card a one-shot deal?  IE, you play it and you get to
>   move the blood one time only.  Or do you play it on a particular
>   vampire and then do you get to move blood every turn?

One shot. One vampire. Into the ash heap.
(Maybe what the FAQ needs is a list of all the cards that aren't
immediately burned.)

>   What clan does the progeny belong to?  We've come up with
>   three different options:
>      1) the clan of the progenitor
>      2) Caitiff
>      3) no clan

Certainly not the clan of the progenitor...  Probably no clan at all.
Would it ever matter if it was a Catiff?

>HAVEN UNCOVERED/BUM'S RUSH
>   Does being attacked via one of these cards tap the defending
>   vampire?

No.  Only acting or blocking causes vampires to tap.

>TELEPAHTIC COUNTER
>   If the bleed is reduced to zero, then the bleed is considered
>   unsuccessful.  Is the bleeding vampire tapped?

Yes, because it took an action.  "considered unsuccessful" basically means
"treat it as if it had been blocked", though no minions will go into combat
as a result.

>MINION TAP
>   Is this card a one-shot deal?  IE, you play it and you get to
>   move the blood one time only.  Or do you play it on a particular
>   vampire and then do you get to move blood every turn?

Yes, it's a one-shot deal.

Major dispute here: you'd have to divorce the card game from the Masquerade.
(Which in the case of this card - maybe it is, but then there'd be no
point in having a separate card - "The Embrace")

The third tradition (from Vampire: TM) states that progeny are the 
responsibility of their makers, and must be conditioned and trained
to be "good" vampires until such time as they are presented to the
prince. Since all the vampires (sans Caitiff) are of the upstanding
Camrilla variety, they should be same clan.

(I think there should actually be a separate rule stating that no
Caitiff could ever hold the title of Prince. It's implicit for 
Justicars.)

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Neither The Embrace nor the Third Tradition say that the vampire so
created is of the same clan as the acting vampire, so they're not.  While
Jyhad is based on Vampire: the Masquerade, VtM really shouldn't be used
as the basis for making rulings on cards.  If you want to play such that
the vampire so created is of the same clan, go for it, but be aware that
that's a house rule, and not what the card says.

(sarcasm on)
Well, let's see what WOULD make for a good ruling on cards. Black's
Legal dictionary? Symbolic logic? The Kama Sutra? No, wait! Loons and their 
Habitats in the British Isles. 
(sarcasm off)

If VtM isn't appropriate source material for producing answers to such
questions, then the game would best be served by removing all VtM references
thus being stripped to bare game mechanics. 

Games are formulations of rules. When rules are placed within a reference
framework, these rules have a 'spirit of interpretation.' 

(When I was a kid, I won a game of Battle of the Bulge by getting X units 
over the Meuse. According to the rules, I won, but my 'bulge' was about 
three hexes wide and the winning units were isolated. Yeah, I won the
game, but my opponent won the *WAR*. I no longer feel that I was the
victor.) 

So, which came first. VtM or the WotC game system? 

To any players who care to comment: 
What are your preferences for resolution such unforseen combinations? 

>but be aware that
>that's a house rule, and not what the card says.

Not a problem. 
1) The "Convocation" doesn't accept Australian membership, so what's
   the point of worrying about convocation rules. 
2) More than a few of WotC rulings are disputed amongst players here.
3) If we play by the card text in every case we'd have an
   unplayable mess (or did the creator of the Chaos Orb really think
   about someone carving the card.) 
4) Army of Rats is ruled redundant. (But that's not what the card says...)
  How about Flak Jackets? How many can a minion use? No limitation is
  set on the card like there is for vehicles or ammo. But as most gun
  enthusiasts (and NFL quarterbacks) will say, "You can't wear two."  

Disclaimer: Never used Progeny/Embrace in a game, but they are in the deck.

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Rick Mc Leod <rxm@mda.com.au> wrote:
>If VtM isn't appropriate source material for producing answers to such
>questions, then the game would best be served by removing all VtM references
>thus being stripped to bare game mechanics. 

While Jyhad is based on Vampire: the Masquerade, pretend it never was,
and just look at the rules and the cards.  If V:tM said that a Saturday
Night Special did more damage than a .44 Magnum, would you play those cards
differently in Jyhad?  The official answer is "No.  SNS says it does 1 damage
and .44 Magnum says it does 2.  Therefore SNS does more damage."  One might
wonder why Jyhad was designed differently from V:tM in that regard, but
the simple fact is that it was.  In this case, The Embrace and Progeny
are not designed as they would work in V:tM.  Why there weren't I don't know;
the point is that they were not.

>So, which came first. VtM or the WotC game system? 

V:tM, but it doesn't really matter, since it has no direct bearing
on how Jyhad works.

>1) The "Convocation" doesn't accept Australian membership, so what's
>   the point of worrying about convocation rules. 

Whether the Convocation accepts anyone's membership is pretty irrelevant
to whether you accept the rules, since it has nothing to say about the
rules of the games it organizes tournaments for, other than imposing
deck construction rules.  Ring of Ma'Ruf is the exception there.

>2) More than a few of WotC rulings are disputed amongst players here.

Not surprising, it happens all the time  ;)

>3) If we play by the card text in every case we'd have an
>   unplayable mess (or did the creator of the Chaos Orb really think
>   about someone carving the card.) 

Occasionally exceptions have to be made, but I don't see how making the
vampire resulting from Embrace or Progency clanless makes the cards
"unplayable".

>4) Army of Rats is ruled redundant. (But that's not what the card says...)

It wasn't "ruled" redundant; errata was issued saying it's redundant.
Basically, in that case, we are telling people to play it other than
as written.

>  How about Flak Jackets? How many can a minion use? No limitation is
>  set on the card like there is for vehicles or ammo. But as most gun
>  enthusiasts (and NFL quarterbacks) will say, "You can't wear two."  

There's an axiom in Magic that "magic doesn't have to make sense".  The rules
have to make sense, but trying to impose a sense of reality on whether certain
card combinations should or shouldn't work (e.g. Sandals of Abdallah on
a Merchant Ship) is a mistake.  The same axiom applies to Jyhad.  It *is*
possible to wear multiple flak jackets, it's just awkward as hell; but
whether it makes sense to do so in reality doesn't have much to do with
whether you can do so in the game.  The card doesn't prohibit a minion
from stacking up multiple vests, so it can.  It's also pretty awkward
to be lugging around two assault rifles, a sawed-off-shotgun, and a 
chainsaw...  Do you have a problem with a minion doing so, like you do
with wearing multiple flak jackets?


Tom Wylie		rec.games.deckmaster Network Representative for
aahz@hal.com			Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Messages.Author: Thomas Doehne
Messages.Body:
Since the game is based on Vampire, the Masquerade, it only
makes sense to look to VtM to resolve open questions.  Where Jyhad
has obvious differences with VtM, of course we play according
to the Jyhad rules. 

   Since it's a question of interpretation as to what happens
when a younger vampire is created with the Third Tradition, 
using VtM as a reference makes sense.  I'd much rather do
that than look strictly at what the card says.  Since, in
this case, the card says nothing whatever, which is why
it's a question at all.

   The created vampire should be of the same clan as its
creator.

--
Tom Doehne
doehne@cse.ogi.edu

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Thomas Doehne <doehne@church.cse.ogi.edu> wrote:
>   Having had extensive experience with Magic, another WotC product,
>I know that plenty of questions slip through playtest.  I would be
>completely unsurprised if the designer just assumed that 'of course'
>a new vampire gets the same clan, and left that info off.

While assumptions do slip through from time to time, they tend to be
of the "of course you can't use this card to do that" variety, and not
"of course this card does that".  In any event, it's dangerous to try
and get inside the designers' heads and try to guess at what their
intentions were, since often people are very wrong about that.  It's best
to just look at the card(s) in question, and the game in question.  Jyhad
is the game in question here, not V:tM, and nothing in the rules or on
the card indicates that the clan would be copied by the fledgling vampire.

>If the
>designer and playtest group had thought it should behave differently
>than Vampire, they would have made the difference explicit on the
>card.  After all, the designer(s) have to be pretty familiar with
>VtM in order to be at all true to the original game...

Yes, but Jyhad rulings should not be made based on V:tM.  For the most part
it should exist in a vacuum.  If it really is ambiguous as to how a card
reads, then looking to see how that concept works in V:tM can be useful
as a tiebreaker, but there is nothing ambiguous about Progeny or The Embrace.
Neither says that the fledgling has a clan, therefore it does not.
Errata might change that, but handwaving about how V:tM works won't.

Messages.Author: Thomas Doehne
Messages.Body:
>
>Yes, but Jyhad rulings should not be made based on V:tM.  For the most part
>it should exist in a vacuum.  

Let's get this straight; Jyhad is a game based on Vampire: the Masquerade.
But the rules for Jyhad should not have anything to do with V:tM?

>If it really is ambiguous as to how a card
>reads, then looking to see how that concept works in V:tM can be useful
>as a tiebreaker, but there is nothing ambiguous about Progeny or The Embrace.
>Neither says that the fledgling has a clan, therefore it does not.
>Errata might change that, but handwaving about how V:tM works won't.

Neither will 'handwaving' that unclear cards should be interpreted however
the Netreps like, without reference to the intellectual foundations of
the game.  Jyhad, unlike Magic, is based on something outside the
game designer's imagination.  Unlike Magic, Jyhad rules do not
exist on an intellectual clean slate.  While you might wish to be
able to interpret Jyhad rules in a vacuumb, you cannot -- V:tM is
the pattern to which Jyhad was woven.  It is a derivative product,
however much you'd like to claim it is completely separate.

Where Jyhad does not conform to the V:tM background, it should be 
very clear about the differences. The Jyhad rules seem to be pretty 
good about that, but this question is one place where it isn't.

--
Tom Doehne
doehne@cse.ogi.edu

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Thomas Doehne <doehne@church.cse.ogi.edu> wrote:
>>Yes, but Jyhad rulings should not be made based on V:tM.  For the most part
>>it should exist in a vacuum.  
>Let's get this straight; Jyhad is a game based on Vampire: the Masquerade.
>But the rules for Jyhad should not have anything to do with V:tM?

One should not have to know how to play Vampire in order
to be able to play Jyhad.  Allowing V:tM to override what the Jyhad rules
and cards say effectively requires one to know how to play Vampire.
Again, if a card is totally ambiguous as to what should happen in a given
situation, then going to V:tM for reference can be helpful, but it should
not be permitted to simply override Jyhad.  Saying that vampire created
via Progeny gets a clan simply because that's what would happen in V:tM
qualifies as allowing V:tM to override Jyhad, which is bad.

>It is a derivative product,
>however much you'd like to claim it is completely separate.

Obviously Jyhad was not designed in a vacuum.  But again, people should
not have to know how to play Vampire to play Jyhad, so Jyhad rulings should
not be overtly based on V:tM.

In article <Cw3uoM.1rH@ucc.su.oz.au>, Rick Mc Leod <rxm@mda.com.au> wrote:
> aahz@hal.COM (Tom Wylie) writes:
>>Jonathan Aiello <ez008723@chip.ucdavis.edu> wrote:
>>>THE THIRD TRADITION: PROGENY
>>>   What clan does the progeny belong to?  We've come up with
>>>   three different options:
>>>      1) the clan of the progenitor
>>>      2) Caitiff
>>>      3) no clan
>>
>>Certainly not the clan of the progenitor...  Probably no clan at all.
>>Would it ever matter if it was a Catiff?
>
>Major dispute here: you'd have to divorce the card game from the Masquerade.
>(Which in the case of this card - maybe it is, but then there'd be no
>point in having a separate card - "The Embrace")

I don't agree.  You can have "Progeny" and "The Embrace" produce new
vampires that, in Jyhad terms, have no clan, while still being
consistant with Vampire: The Masquerade.

You've got to remember that Jyhad is far more abstract than Vampire.
What does a clan symbol on a Jyhad card *mean*?  It doesn't just mean
that the vampire is descended from the same antideluvian founder as
other vampires with that symbol.  It means that they have enough
STATUS in that clan to invoke it's special privelages -- voting for a
Justicar, invoking special clan allies, et cetera.  It means they're
an integral part of the political structure of that clan.

A Neonate wouldn't have the clan status to do these things yet.  So,
while in Vampire terms they're of the clan of their sire, in *JYHAD*
terms, they aren't of any clan at all.  It makes perfect sense to me.

Neither Archon nor Camarilla Exemplary stays in play, but rather just have
an effect on the vampire.  Thus their effects would not wear off if the person
putting that effect into play was ousted.  People will typically leave these
cards out to remind everyone of the effect, but technically they are
not in play.

I don't see any override. It's a logical inference based on common sense
and VtM. Clans are not an award. Vampires can not change clan. They
can be cast out of society. They can be orphaned. If I believed that VtM
should override Jyhad, then I'd print out little Thaumaturgy symbols
for Wake with Evening's Freshness and stick them on everyone's cards. 

>
>Obviously Jyhad was not designed in a vacuum.  But again, people should
>not have to know how to play Vampire to play Jyhad, so Jyhad rulings should
>not be overtly based on V:tM.
>
Who said anything about overt basis on VtM? I believe it's supporting
evidence, but, I was a member of my clan the day I became progeny. That
is common sense. It didn't require a written decree (and there still
aren't any in many parts of the world.)  

No one has to know anything about VtM to come to that conclusion. This
leads to a bigger question: Does the "Jyhad Rules Committee" intend to
take into account VtM when making such decisions, or are they more likely
to be vacuum based? Admittedly, many cards have no relationship to VtM
at all (Fake Out, etc.), and questions of this type are few and far
between (Rotschreck, Titles, and this are the only ones that come to
mind so far. It should probably also be noted that the one vampire,
one title position has strong basis in VtM, but no support whatsoever
in the Jyhad rules - according to which a single vampire could be
Prince of All Cities and Justicar of her Clan, and a primogen 
simultaneously.)
